sections.h2: Where are deeds recorded in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Division of Real Estate, which sits in Room 101 of the County Office Building at 542 Forbes Avenue in Pittsburgh. The division does the recorder's work in this county, and it also collects the state and local transfer taxes.

The counter keeps weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For questions, call 412-350-4636 and choose Option 2. The recording page says most documents can be eRecorded online, so a title company in another city can submit a deed without anyone walking into Room 101.

A homeowner who sells in Allegheny County will usually never visit the counter. The title agent prepares the deed, records it, and sends the tax and fee payments that the division requires.

sections.h2: What does the Allegheny County Division of Real Estate charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The standard recording fee for a deed is $200.00, and a mortgage costs the same, under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. Large documents add charges only when they pass 30 parcels or 30 indexed names.

Allegheny County recording fees effective January 1, 2026
Document typeStandard fee
Deed and deed related documents$200.00
Mortgage and mortgage related documents$200.00
Power of attorney$50.00
Notary public bond and commission$80.00
Financial statement$175.00
Military service dischargeNo fee

Source: the Division of Real Estate recording fee sheet. Each parcel past 30 on a deed adds $10.00, and each indexed name past 30 adds $5.00. Deed related documents include leases, rights of way, declarations of trust, oil and gas documents and sewage permits, all at the same $200.00.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a sale in Allegheny County?
sections.html:
It runs from 2% to 5% of the price depending on where the house is, and 1% of that goes to the state. The remainder goes to the municipality and the school district that cover the property.

The division collects every layer of the tax at recording, with one check for transfer tax and a second check for the recording fee. The county's own worked examples show the spread on a $40,000 sale:

  • A house in Shaler Township pays 1% to the state, 0.5% to the township and 0.5% to Shaler Area School District, for $800.00 in total.
  • A house in the City of Pittsburgh pays 1% to the state, 3% to the city and 1% to Pittsburgh School District, for $2,000.00 in total.

Scale those percentages to a real price and the difference is large. On a $200,000 sale, 2% is $4,000 and 5% is $10,000. Ask the closing agent for the exact municipal and school rates before the settlement statement is final.

When no price appears on the deed, or when an exemption applies, a Statement of Value on Pennsylvania form REV-183 is required. Certain family transfers can skip the form if the deed carries a sentence explaining the relationship. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, at 717-783-8104, handles exemption questions.

sections.h2: What formatting rules apply to an Allegheny County deed?
sections.html:
A deed must be typed in black ink on white or manila sheets, 8 1/2 by 11 inches or 8 1/2 by 14 inches, in a font of at least 10 points. Continuous paper is rejected.

  • Leave a one inch margin at the top of the first page for the certification stamp.
  • Print a name and a full address with zip code in the Record and Mail to area, outside that top margin.
  • Handwriting is limited to signatures, acknowledgments and a few listed exceptions.
  • Keep out tape, glue, staples, correction fluid and highlighting.
  • Double-sided pages are fine, though each side that carries text counts as a separate page for the fee.

The same page sets a formatting rule for the Certificate of Residence, and the county publishes content requirements for each document type separately.

sections.h2: How can I pay recording fees in Allegheny County?
sections.html:
Paying in person takes cash, a business check, a money order or a cashier's check. Personal checks, debit cards and credit cards are refused.

Firms that record often can open a draw down account in the office during business hours, which saves the trip to the counter with a check each time. The recording page lists online payment as an option, and the county posts a separate sheet for copies and their associated fees.

Anyone who sees an unfamiliar deed or mortgage filed against their property can use the county's web form to report suspected deed or mortgage fraud.

sections.h2: Where does the common level ratio come into a deed?
sections.html:
The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue issues a new Common Level Ratio factor for each county every year, effective July 1, and the Division of Real Estate links to it from its transfer tax page. The factor sits in the same list of helpful items as the Statement of Value, so a filer working on a gift or low-price deed will see both together.

The county's appeal board, meanwhile, lists 49.3% as the common level ratio for the 2027 tax year, applied to current market value in assessment appeals that began in September 2026. A ratio near 49% signals that county assessments, frozen to a 2012 base year, run well below current market prices. Ask the closing agent which figure belongs on the Statement of Value before the deed is signed.

sections.h2: What is Allegheny County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Allegheny County covers 745 square miles, and the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet at Downtown Pittsburgh to form the Ohio. The Youghiogheny River joins the Monongahela at McKeesport, about ten miles to the southeast. With 130 municipalities, the county has more local governments than any other in Pennsylvania, and neighboring municipalities can carry different transfer tax rates.

The Census Bureau counted 1,225,035 residents in its July 2025 estimate, second in the state behind Philadelphia, and it lists 614,484 housing units.

sections.h2: What should an Allegheny County seller check before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
1. Confirm the municipality and school district, since those two set most of the transfer tax.
  2. Review the deed against the formatting rules above so the division does not reject it.
  3. Decide who pays transfer tax; the Department of Revenue says both grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable for the tax, so settle the split in writing.
  4. Choose eRecording or hand delivery, and for hand delivery plan on a business check, cashier's check, money order or cash.

Buyers of rental houses have a second step. Effective September 18, 2026, Act 29 of 2026 requires a new owner of non-owner-occupied real estate to send contact details to the county's chief assessor within 30 days of purchase, and a knowingly false filing can bring a fine of up to $500. A seller who is handing a tenant-occupied house to an investor can mention that duty to the buyer.

faqs.q: What is the standard recording fee for a deed in Allegheny County?
faqs.a: It is $200.00 for a deed and for a mortgage under the fee sheet effective January 1, 2026. Parcels beyond 30 add $10.00 each and indexed names beyond 30 add $5.00 each.

faqs.q: Does Allegheny County take personal checks or cards at the recording counter?
faqs.a: No. The Division of Real Estate does not accept personal checks, debit cards or credit cards. It takes cash, business checks, money orders, cashier's checks and draw down accounts, and online payment exists for eRecorded filings.

faqs.q: Why is the transfer tax so different between Pittsburgh and the suburbs?
faqs.a: The 1% state share is constant, while the municipal and school district shares change by location. On the county's $40,000 example, Shaler Township totals 2% and the City of Pittsburgh totals 5%.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded without visiting Room 101?
faqs.a: Yes, the county says most documents can be eRecorded online. For hand delivery, the address is 542 Forbes Avenue, Room 101, and the counter keeps weekday hours.

faqs.q: Does a military discharge cost anything to record in Allegheny County?
faqs.a: No. Military service discharge papers, street or alley vacations and ordinances are listed with no recording fee.
